subject: Access controls & support access - follow up from today's call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintrust.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 4, 2026 at 09:02 AM PDT
Subject: Access controls & support access - follow up from today's call

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for your time on the call earlier — great discussion. Per our conversation, here’s a concise recap of the access controls and support/access-related items we covered, plus proposed next steps.

Summary (what we covered)
- RBAC model: role-based access with least-privilege by default. Roles can be scoped at org / project / route level (Owner, Admin, Developer, Viewer, Auditor, Support).
- Support access: Just-in-time (JIT) support access for live troubleshooting, approved by your admin. All sessions are time-bound and scoped.
- Break-glass: Emergency escalation path that requires a documented break-glass request, supervisor approval, 2FA, and full audit logging.
- Data handling: PII minimization recommendations, customizable data retention policies, and optional in-region data residency (US, EU).
- Logging: Audit logs (change history, admin actions, support sessions) are immutable, tamper-evident, and exportable to your S3/Cloud bucket; retention configurable.

Ask / Next steps
1) Confirm whether you want the security deep-dive with your engineering/security team + our SE (Aditya) this Friday afternoon or early next week.
2) Share any specific examples of the PII/objects you want excluded from long-term retention so we can propose retention rules.
3) We’ll send the RBAC & support access docs + SOC2 summary (attached).

Attachments: redwood-rbac-overview.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

If that all looks right I’ll loop in Aditya for the technical deep-dive and schedule the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Marissa — that summary is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we set the deep-dive: 

1) Break-glass: can you confirm whether break-glass access requires a signed approval each time, or if there is a delegated emergency approver pool we can configure? We need to ensure this meets our internal audit requirements.
2) Support access: does Redwood require console-level access for engineers, or do you use an agent-based session proxy? We want to avoid sharing long-lived credentials.
3) Data residency: we need confirmation that data processing and persistent storage can be limited to US regions only (no EU fallback) for this account.
4) Logs: can you provide a sample audit-log export (redacted) so our SIEM team can validate schema / fields?

Looping in Sam (security engineer) to triage any technical asks and procurement for next steps.

—Elena
Elena Morales

Subject: Re: Access controls & support access - follow up from today's call

Hi Elena — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve attached a couple of docs and a sample log export.

1) Break-glass: You can configure a small pool of emergency approvers (delegated approvers). By default we log the identity of the approver and require a written justification captured in the ticket. For higher-assurance workflows, we can require an explicit signed approval per event (configurable per-org).

2) Support access: Redwood uses an ephemeral-access proxy — we do not share long-lived support credentials. Support engineers request JIT access, which must be approved by your admin. Sessions are recorded and scoped to specific namespaces/resources.

3) Data residency: Yes — we can pin processing and persistent storage to a US-only region for your account (no EU failover). We’ll include the account-level residency config in the deep-dive.

4) Logs: attached a redacted sample audit-logs-sample.csv showing fields exported to S3; schema includes timestamp, actor_email, action_type, resource_path, before/after metadata, session_id, and source_ip.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, support-access-process.docx, audit-logs-sample.csv

Proposed next step: Technical deep-dive with Aditya and your security team — does Friday 3/6 at 2:00 PM PT work for you? If not, please propose a couple of windows next week.

Thanks — looping Aditya in for any technical additions.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Elena — quick technical notes to supplement Marissa's answers: 

- RBAC granularity: roles are additive and can be scoped to org/project/model/route. You can create custom roles via the console or API; least-privilege templates available (e.g., ReadOnlyInference, ModelAdmin, BillingViewer).

- Support access / break-glass flow (high level):
  1) Support creates JIT request with rationale and scope (resources + expiry).
  2) Customer admin(s) receive approval request via console/Email and can approve or deny.
  3) If approved, an ephemeral access token is minted (time-limited, scoped). Access is recorded and streamed to the customer's audit bucket; session recording is available for support sessions.
  4) Break-glass: if an approver is unavailable, the emergency approver pool can approve with two-person validation; all break-glass events require post-event justification and are flagged in the audit pipeline for your SOC review.

- Logging & retention: default audit log retention is 90 days; we support custom retention policies up to several years on a per-account basis. Logs are write-once in the audit store; exports are delivered as compressed CSV/JSON to your S3.

- Additional controls: IP allowlists for control-plane access, SCIM for provisioning, and optional KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys.

I can walk through a sample JIT request and show live session recording playback during the deep-dive. Friday 3/6 2:00 PM PT works on our side — send calendar invite and we’ll confirm.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
